# 1 Clement Chapter 59 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 59

---

## Council Notes

**On "beloved child" / "beloved servant" (vv.1–3):** EMET/PNEUMA: "child." LOGOS: "servant." The Greek *pais* means both "child" and "servant/slave." This ambiguity is theologically significant — it echoes the Servant Songs of Isaiah (LXX *pais* = the Suffering Servant) as well as the Father-Son relationship. Both renderings have legitimate support. SOPHIA rules: use "child" in v.1 and v.3 (reflecting the intimate divine-human relationship), noting the servant dimension in the council notes. This is the earliest extant Christian liturgical use of *pais* for Christ.

**On poetic lineation (vv.2–3):** PNEUMA formats vv.2–3 as poetry. This is the correct approach for the Great Prayer. The long accumulation of divine titles and petitions in v.2 is unmistakably hymnic in Greek — the attributive participial clauses pile up in a doxological catalogue. SOPHIA affirms poetic formatting for vv.2–3 while maintaining prose for v.1 (which is discursive).

**On "Finder of spirits" / "sole Finder of spirits" (v.2):** All agents preserve this unusual divine title: *pneumatōn ktistēs kai episkopos* (lit. "creator and overseer of spirits"). The title "Finder of spirits" (*monos heuretēs pneumatōn*) is distinctive and should be preserved exactly.

**On v.3's intercession list:** The list — afflicted, lowly, fallen, sick, wanderers, hungry, captives, weak, faint-hearted — is a remarkably comprehensive intercession. It anticipates later Christian intercessory prayer forms. The parallelism should be preserved precisely.

**On "Succourer" (LOGOS v.3):** LOGOS uses "Succourer" (from *boēthēs*). EMET: "Helper." PNEUMA: "Helper." "Helper" is more accessible while still carrying the Greek sense. Retained.

---

**59:1** But if any should be disobedient to what has been said by him through us, let them know that they will entangle themselves in transgression and no small peril. As for us, we shall be innocent of this sin, and we will pray with earnest entreaty and supplication that the Creator of all things may keep intact the full number of his elect throughout the whole world, through his beloved child Jesus Christ, through whom he called us from darkness to light, from ignorance to the knowledge of the glory of his name.

**59:2** *Grant us, Lord, to set our hope upon your name —*
*the primal source of all creation.*
*Open the eyes of our hearts to know you:*

*you who alone are the Highest among the highest,*
*the Holy One resting among the holy;*
*you who humble the insolence of the proud,*
*who scatter the counsels of the nations,*
*who exalt the humble and abase the lofty;*
*you who make rich and make poor;*
*you who kill and make alive —*
*you alone, the Finder of spirits*
*and the God of all flesh;*
*you who look upon the depths*
*and observe the works of men;*
*the Helper of those in peril,*
*the Savior of those in despair,*
*the Creator and Guardian of every spirit;*
*you who multiply the nations upon the earth*
*and out of all have chosen those who love you*
*through Jesus Christ, your beloved child —*
*through whom you have instructed us,*
*sanctified us, and honored us.*

**59:3** *We beseech you, Master: be our helper and defender.*
*Save those among us who are in affliction.*
*Raise up those who are lowly.*
*Lift up those who have fallen.*
*Heal the sick.*
*Turn back the wanderers of your people.*
*Feed the hungry.*
*Release the captives.*
*Strengthen the feeble.*
*Give courage to the faint-hearted.*

*Let all the nations know you,*
*that you alone are God,*
*and that Jesus Christ is your child,*
*and that we are your people*
*and the sheep of your pasture.*

---

*— SOPHIA*
